thread:
incident-bot: [SEV2] p99 latency spike on production inference cluster us-west-1 - alert triggered (streaming.tail.stalls > 10/min)
Ivy (oncall): acked, paging team. I'm on it. Can someone grab p95/p99 numbers and top affected routes? :eyes: 
Sam (sre): grabbing dashboard now. quick numbers: p95=420ms -> 1.1s, p99=580ms -> 3.2s over last 10m. streaming stalls metric jumped from ~2/min to ~28/min. Error rate low, no CPU/GPU OOMs.
Harper (runtime): seeing a bunch of KV cache eviction logs simultaneously across nodes. sample from node runtime-12:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=4212] INFO kv_cache: slab_eviction: slab_id=9 evict_bytes=524288 evict_entries=1024 policy=LRU
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z runtime[pid=4212] WARN kv_cache: prefill_queue_len=142 decode_queue_len=18 prefill_vs_decode_ratio=7.9
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z runtime[pid=4212] ERROR streaming: stall_detected span_ms=2345 tail_seq=98765 reason=kv_prefill_block
```
Maya (infra): infra metrics show sudden increase in `kv_prefill_io_ms` and `kv_fragmentation_ratio` on several shards: frag_ratio jumped 0.24 -> 0.72 on shard group sg-3 in us-west-1. Eviction throughput also spiked.
Casey (support): we have 3 customer reports about slow streaming responses since ~13:58, two enterprise customers - one on Dedicated. Notified them we are investigating.
Ivy (oncall): sounds like KV cache pressure / fragmentation causing prefill queue to dominate decode, leading to streaming tail stalls. Next steps: 1) quick mitigation to reduce customer impact, 2) deeper triage. Proposal: pause eviction on most-impacted shards and route a subset of traffic to fallback model variant. Thoughts?
Sam (sre): agree with pause eviction short-term. On runtime nodes we can flip `kv.eviction.enabled=false` via config rollout per-pool. Doing a controlled toggle on pool=prod-usw1-robin. Will verify memory pressure before/after.
Harper (runtime): preparing small hotfix to rebalance slab allocations and reduce prefill prioritization. Hotfix contains two changes: increase slab_budget for active shards and lower `prefill_priority` weight. Patch ready to apply to canary nodes.
ops-bot: deploy request received: `/deploy runtime/kv-hotfix to canary` queued. Confirm to proceed with canary rollout?
Ivy (oncall): proceed with canary. Sam, please apply eviction=false on most impacted 5 shards first (non-Dedicated if possible). Harper, once canary looks stable, we roll to rest. Casey, please send interim customer update mentioning we're mitigating and may route some traffic briefly.
Sam (sre): eviction=false toggled on shards: sg-3-a, sg-3-b, sg-4-a. Commands used:
```
# control plane API
curl -s -XPOST "https://controlplane.prod.redwood/api/v1/shards/sg-3-a/config" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"kv.eviction.enabled": false}'
```
Sam (sre): monitoring memory: resident set rose ~6% on those nodes but within headroom. immediate streaming stalls down from 28/min to ~6/min in 2m. p99 trending down to ~1.2s.
Harper (runtime): canary patch applied to runtime-9. Prefill_vs_decode ratio dropped from 7.9 -> 1.6 on that node. No errors so far. Will start rolling to rest of prod-usw1 pool with 2-min observation windows.
Casey (support): sent note to customers: "We're applying mitigations to reduce latency; may see short routing changes. We expect improvement within 10–20 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and next steps."
Alex (eng): quick question — any chance this was triggered by a traffic pattern change? I see a spike in long-context prompts from a few customers around 13:55. Could be working set blowup.
Maya (infra): correlating request histograms now. There was a 3x increase in average seq length for route `/v1/stream` from one tenant (tenant-42). That tenant's traffic is mostly on Dedicated pool dp-7, which had higher frag_ratio too.
Harper (runtime): interesting: Dedicated pool has slightly different slab sizing. Eviction was thrashing dedicated slabs -> prefills queued while decode threads blocked on KV fetch. For Dedicated we need a different mitigation: either move those tenants to a different pool or temporarily throttle seq length via rate-limit.
Ivy (oncall): topology decision: for Dedicated customers affected, coordinate with account team for temporary routing. Sam/Maya, can you create a short-lived ingress rule to route tenant-42 to fallback pool `dp-7-fallback` which has larger slab budget?
Sam (sre): created routing rule and added rate-limit on tenant-42 for long-context requests (max_seq=1024). Routing change applied at 14:12:45.
ops-bot: route change applied: tenant-42 -> dp-7-fallback (id: route-9876).
Sam (sre): after routing change, dp-7 frag_ratio dropped from 0.72 -> 0.36 and p99 for that tenant improved from 4.8s -> 1.4s. Overall cluster p99 at 14:18 = 980ms.
Harper (runtime): followup fixes: 1) longer-term config change to increase slab allocation per-Dedicated-customer tiers, 2) add prefill prioritization heuristic to avoid prefill floods, 3) add metric `kv.prefill_blocking_fraction` for alerting.
Ivy (oncall): can we get a temporary slab bump for prod-usw1 while we schedule a proper config change? If yes, do it after post-canary.
Maya (infra): issuing quick slab bump via controlplane: `kv_slab_bytes += 25%` for prod-usw1. Command executed at 14:22:05.
```
POST /api/v1/pools/prod-usw1/scale
{ "kv_slab_bytes_delta_pct": 25 }
```
Harper (runtime): after bump, memory headroom still okay, prefill queue stabilized. Rolling patch to all runtime nodes in prod-usw1 completed at 14:28. Observability shows streaming stalls back to baseline ~2/min and p99 ~650ms.
Casey (support): updated customers: improvement confirmed for tenants A,B,C; tenant-42 shows restored perf with fallback routing. Customers asked for timeline for permanent fix.
Alex (eng): capturing reproducer: I'll run load test against a canary cluster to reproduce prefill surge with long-context traffic. Will link results here.
Ivy (oncall): thanks team. Summary so far: root cause initial hypothesis = KV cache fragmentation + eviction thrash due to sudden long-context traffic bump causing prefill vs decode imbalance and blocking streaming decode threads. Mitigations applied: (1) pause eviction on hot shards, (2) canary runtime patch to reduce prefill priority, (3) slab budget bump for prod-usw1, (4) route heavy tenant to fallback pool + rate-limit. Impact: p99 improved from 3.2s -> ~650ms, streaming stalls reduced to baseline. Customer impact: limited to 3 reported customers (one Dedicated) — support notified.
Harper (runtime): next actions (owners):
- Add prefill prioritization heuristic (owner: Harper/runtime) - ETA 3d
- Config templates for Dedicated slab sizing (owner: Maya/infra + Product) - ETA 5d
- Add `kv.prefill_blocking_fraction` alert and refine thresholds (owner: Sam/sre) - ETA 2d
- Repro test with long-context traffic (owner: Alex/eng) - ETA 1d
Ivy (oncall): passing handoff to Sam (next oncall) at 14:32. Sam — please monitor for 2h and kick off postmortem doc. Postmortem owner: Ivy.
Sam (sre): taking handoff. I'll create incident ticket INC-2026-042 and draft mitigation timeline. Will post link when ready.
Ivy (oncall): final note — keep customer comms coordinated with Casey. Add any new findings to the ticket. Good job everyone :tada:
